clue.text: Quickest way to pay a bunch of cow hands?

definitions.text: Quickest way to pay a bunch of cow hands?

parts.words: Quickest way to pay a bunch of cow hands?
parts.note: paying immediately in money on the spot is the fastest settlement, and the phrase also hints at cattle being handed cash

explanation.surface: A rancher wonders how to settle wages fastest with a crew of farmhands.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue simply describes paying up front in money; the cowhands are colour for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying in money at the moment of purchase is the most immediate form of settlement.

clue.text: Delectable option

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, of fine quality, as in a select cut of meat
as a noun, a selection or alternative

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both top-quality (an adjective for fine food) and an alternative picked from several.

clue.text: Part or all of a jacket?

definitions.text: Part or all of a jacket?

parts.words: Part or all of a jacket?
parts.note: an arm covering is part of a coat, while a record's cardboard cover is the whole jacket of an LP

explanation.surface: A tailor wonders whether one piece makes up the whole garment.
explanation.walkthrough: A record cover is called a jacket in the US, so the arm piece of a coat is part of a jacket, and a record cover is all of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm piece of a coat shares its name with the cardboard cover of a vinyl record.

clue.text: Stops a bed being turned over to the Royal Society?

indicators.note: turned over tells us the words a bed are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: RS is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's science academy

explanation.surface: A bed is upended and donated to a learned scientific institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning bars from entry; 'to the' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar or exclude someone is to stop them from entering or taking part.

clue.text: Puddled wine-lovers regarded as gluttons

indicators.note: puddled means muddled or confused, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Drunken wine enthusiasts are dismissed as greedy overeaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puddled' (muddled, drunk) is the anagram signal for the ten letters of WINE-LOVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is also called the glutton, from its reputation for voracious eating.

clue.text: Vinegary star with face twitch

parts.note: an ace is a star performer, an expert
a tic is an involuntary spasm, often of the face

explanation.surface: A sour-tempered celebrity has a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the main component of vinegar, so the adjective describes something vinegar-like.

clue.text: Talks to one hundred headwear manufacturers

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
hatters make hats

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a hundred milliners at a convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter is to talk rapidly and idly, so the verb fits 'talks'.

clue.text: Go off and become cynical, possibly

definitions.meaning: of milk or food, to spoil
of a person, to grow bitter or disillusioned

explanation.definitionFit: Milk that spoils curdles, and a person who grows embittered has metaphorically curdled in the same way.

clue.text: Redesigned sidecars that let Troilus down

indicators.note: redesigned signals that the letters of sidecars are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Motorcycle sidecars were remodelled, which disappointed someone named Troilus.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Trojan legend retold by Chaucer and Shakespeare, Troilus is betrayed by his lover, who deserts him for the Greek Diomedes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Troy story she is the faithless lover who betrays Troilus for Diomedes.

clue.text: Presuming far too much?

parts.note: presuming in the sense of being forward or presumptuous, and to excess

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of taking liberties well beyond what is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excessively forward or presumptuous is having too much daring or cheek.

clue.text: Young Lawrence and I break a rule somehow

indicators.note: I breaks into the rearranged letters, sitting inside them
somehow suggests the letters of a rule are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A boy owns up to breaking one of the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns A RULE into LAURE, and 'break' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The diminutive is the pet form of the name, as one would call a boy.

clue.text: Insurance allowed on a bed, perhaps

parts.note: insurance gives cover against loss
let means permitted

explanation.surface: An insurance policy is approved for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the thing that lies on top of a bed.

clue.text: TASS is organised for a stoppage

indicators.note: organised suggests putting the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Soviet news agency, taken as written

explanation.surface: The Russian news agency has been arranged to cause a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: TASS was the official news agency of the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of equilibrium where nothing moves is a halt or standstill.

clue.text: Instructions ultimately given for the 14 at the tavern

parts.note: ultimately means finally, at the end
orders are commands

explanation.surface: A landlord's final directions are given at closing time in an inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is FINAL ROUND: in a British pub the barman calls for the final drinks before closing.
explanation.definitionFit: The barman's call for the final drinks of the night is the closing round at a pub.

clue.text: The end of the fight at the top of the ladder

definitions.meaning: the closing session of a boxing bout

definitions.text: at the top of the ladder
definitions.meaning: the deciding contest at the head of a knockout competition

explanation.definitionFit: The closing session of a bout and the deciding stage of a tournament share this name.

clue.text: A simple brew for the valetudinarian

definitions.text: A simple brew for the valetudinarian

parts.words: A simple brew for the valetudinarian
parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant, and an invalid might take a brewed drink made from such plants

explanation.surface: A sickly person is offered a basic homemade drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' is an old noun for a medicinal plant, and a valetudinarian is a person anxious about their health.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink brewed from plants such as dandelion or nettle is a folk tonic for invalids.

clue.text: Badly tailored image-worshipper

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of tailored are messed about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone who worships appearances is wearing an ill-fitting suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who venerates statues or images as gods is the classic worshipper of false icons.

clue.text: Domestic batting learnt haphazardly

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: haphazardly means at random, so the letters of learnt are jumbled

explanation.surface: A home cricketer has picked up batting skills in a random fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic affairs, as opposed to foreign ones, are those inside a country.

clue.text: Mischievous heathen god naturally featuring in Hardy's novels

indicators.note: mischievous suggests unruly behaviour, so the letters of heathen god are scrambled

explanation.surface: A naughty pagan deity turns up in Thomas Hardy's fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy's fictional Wessex includes this wild heath, the setting of The Return of the Native; 'naturally' hints it is a landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild stretch of moorland is the brooding setting of Thomas Hardy's The Return of the Native.

clue.text: A striking piece of minor devilry

definitions.meaning: a collision or blow, as a noun
the deed of a little demon, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a collision, and split in two it is the deed of a small demon.

clue.text: Dutch courage!

parts.note: boldness got from drink comes out of a container of liquor, and in British slang the container's name also means nerve

explanation.surface: Someone needs a drink to steel their nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the word means nerve or courage, and drink-fuelled bravery comes from a glass container of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang word for nerve is also the vessel from which drunken bravado is poured.

clue.text: Bumble bee dissected by frenzied lad

indicators.note: dissected by means the first word is cut open with the other piece put inside
frenzied suggests wild movement, so the letters of lad are shuffled

explanation.surface: A bumblebee is cut up by an excitable boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bumble' is not the insect: Mr Bumble is the pompous parish officer in Dickens's Oliver Twist, and 'frenzied' scrambles the short word that the insect's name surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Bumble in Oliver Twist is the workhouse's parish officer, the archetypal pompous church official.

clue.text: Place where a soldier may sleep like a log

definitions.text: Place where a soldier may sleep

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both quarters assigned to a soldier and a chunk of firewood.

clue.text: Straightforward language about border flower

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: prose is plain everyday writing, not verse
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Plain writing describes the flowers at the edge of a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a pale yellow spring-flowering plant of hedgerows and woods.

clue.text: Get in a pie? For this, maybe

definitions.text: Get in a pie? For this, maybe

indicators.note: in printing, pie is type jumbled together, so the letters of get in a are mixed up

explanation.surface: A recipe suggests putting something inside a pastry, perhaps to be consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: Printer's pie is spilt, jumbled type, so 'pie' signals an anagram; and a pie is made to be consumed, which makes the clue whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie exists to be consumed, so the whole clue points at consuming food.

clue.text: Left for dead, apparently

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both having gone away and, euphemistically, deceased.

clue.text: Very seldom an artist to depend on

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
rely means count on

explanation.surface: A painter is hardly ever someone you can count on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens infrequently happens only seldom.

clue.text: It was differentiated before, so to speak

indicators.note: differentiated means made different, so the letters of it was are reordered

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before

explanation.surface: A past event was distinguished from what came earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a filler meaning 'in a manner of speaking'.
